content: When oral microbiota products, which contain bacterial spores, are co-administered with antibacterial agents, the efficacy of the microbiota therapy may be reduced due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction occurs because antibacterial agents can inhibit the activity or survival of the bacterial spores present in the microbiota product. To minimize this risk, it is recommended to complete any ongoing antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days prior to initiating oral microbiota therapy. Specific antibiotics, such as rifamycin, rifaximin, sarecycline, streptomycin, sulbactam/durlobactam, sulfadiazine, sulfanilamide, sulfisoxazole, sulopenem, tebipenem, tedizolid, telavancin, tetracycline, tigecycline, tobramycin, trimethoprim, vancomycin, and others, have been shown to decrease the effects of oral microbiota products through this mechanism. In such cases, it is advised to avoid these antibiotics or consider using alternative drugs to prevent reduced efficacy of the microbiota therapy. This recommendation extends to a wide range of antibacterial agents, including aminoglycosides (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin), beta-lactams (e.g., amoxicillin, ampicillin, cefepime, ceftriaxone), macrolides (e.g., azithromycin, erythromycin), fluoroquinolones (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, demeclocycline), and other classes of antibiotics. For each of these agents, the same precaution applies: complete the antibiotic course 2 to 4 days before starting oral microbiota therapy, or use an alternative treatment to avoid compromising the therapeutic effects of the microbiota product.
